title: Fix the Mistake (B1–B2)
description: Spot and correct classic English grammar mistakes before your rival team steals!

questions.q: Fix: "He don’t know the answer."
Fix: "I am agree with your idea."
Fix: "She has went to the market."
questions.a: She has gone to the market.

questions.q: Fix: "We discussed about the project."
Fix: "If it will rain, we will stay inside."
questions.a: If it rains, we will stay inside.

questions.q: Fix: "Can you give me an advice?"
questions.a: Can you give me some advice? (or a piece of advice)

questions.q: Fix: "Despite of the traffic, we arrived early."
questions.a: Despite the traffic, we arrived early.

questions.q: Fix: "I am looking forward to see you."
questions.a: I am looking forward to seeing you.

questions.q: Fix: "Everyone in the class are excited."
questions.a: Everyone in the class is excited.

questions.q: Fix: "She is more taller than her brother."
questions.a: She is taller than her brother.

questions.q: Fix: "He suggested me to take a break."
questions.a: He suggested that I take a break.

questions.q: Fix: "Neither the teacher nor the students was ready."
questions.a: Neither the teacher nor the students were ready.

title: Speak & Score Prompts
description: Open-ended speaking challenges (no fixed answer) great for fluency & full-sentence practice.

questions.q: Describe your favorite meal using at least 3 adjectives.
Tell the class about one thing you did last weekend.
Would you rather live near the beach or in the mountains? Why?
Give a friend two pieces of advice for learning English faster.
Name 3 things you always pack in your school bag or backpack.
Compare a bicycle and a car using two comparative sentences.
If you won a free plane ticket anywhere, where would you go?
Describe your classroom without using the words "desk" or "chair".
What is one new skill you would like to learn this year?
Say one polite request you would use in a restaurant.
